title: McGill 1993: csa anatomical of latissimus dorsi at T8-T9 (M, supine)

imaging.modality: MRI Philips Gyroscan, spin echo TR 500 TE 20
imaging.plane: transverse slices (scanner axial, trunk in anatomic supine position); for each level the slice closest to the disc centre (within 5 mm)
imaging.level_definition: disc level: column labelled with the vertebra above the disc (e.g. "L3" = L3/L4), inferred from Table 5 which uses disc labels

quantity.name: csa_anatomical
quantity.definition: anatomical cross-sectional area of the muscle in the image plane (as cut, not corrected for fibre direction)

source.authors: McGill SM, Santaguida L, Stevens J
source.sample: 15 young men; healthy, no history of disabling back disease

how_to_simulate: Pose the model supine (lying; lordosis as when lying, no gravity load on trunk).

Select all latissimus dorsi fascicles whose path crosses the plane at T8-T9 (transverse slices (scanner axial, trunk in anatomic supine position); for each level the slice closest to the disc centre (within 5 mm)), one side.
Sum their PCSA; divide each PCSA by cos(angle between fascicle and plane normal) to get anatomical CSA.
Compare the one-side total with the measured mean +/- SD (bilateral sums are labelled side=bilateral_sum).

subject_model.source: Methods (SD age 3.6, weight 10.7, height 6.8); disc area Table 2

protocol.notes: Raw area in the transverse MRI slice. Erector mass and abdominal wall areas include intermuscular spaces (slightly larger than the sum of components).

extraction.check_notes: Every cell transcribed from rendered pages 175-176 (PDF text layer is OCR-garbled); re-checked column alignment against the column headers.
